title: Loop gain, phase margin and gain margin across the DR-002 C_out/ESR window (0-50mA)
claim: Substantiates spec/target-spec.md's ratified "Stability" row (stable 0-50 mA over the ratified C_out/ESR window; PM >= 45 deg, GM >= 10 dB worst corner) against the issue-#25 current-mirror-OTA revision of the LDO core-regulation loop (design/ldo_3v3in_1v8out.sch). Both the spec row and the window are ratified by issue #1 / DR-006 -- the window being DR-002's C_eff 0.33-4.7 uF / ESR 0-500 mOhm / no-minimum-ESR posture -- so the bounds below cite them verbatim rather than an invented final limit. What DR-002 ratified is the window's numeric boundaries; its no-minimum-ESR *stability claim* is only partially substantiated, per DR-006's own disclosed 0 mA-corner gap, which is exactly what this testbench measures. This is also the testbench DR-002 sequenced itself in front of: DR-002 states its no-minimum-ESR posture stays an unverified claim 'until a loop-gain sim/ record exists', and names the low-C_eff/low-ESR corner as the one that has to be shown. Method: closed-loop injection at VREF with the loop gain recovered as T = X/(1-X), X = v(xldo.fb) -- see the testbench schematic's header for the derivation, and for the one approximation it makes (input-pair path asymmetry, a fraction of a degree at these crossovers). As of #179 all seven points are seeded per sim/README.md's initial-condition contract (#171): the testbench carries a .nodeset card seeding the three branch-defining nodes (VOUT=1.8, FB=1.2, N_FBB=0.6), which ngspice applies to EVERY operating-point solve in the deck -- including the one each `ac` performs for itself -- so no point linearizes around an unconstrained Newton solve. `.ic` would not have done this: ngspice honours `.ic` only for the transient operating point, so it is inert in an ac-only deck. Only the branch-defining nodes are seeded, because a .nodeset card is a single static card applied to all seven points while every other node's value is set by the operating current: the eleven-node seed from sim/ic-screen-125c-b (125C/50mA values) was measured to drag ss/-40C/3.63V's 1mA point onto a non-regulating branch (VOUT=3.633V=VIN) and to raise solver diagnostics on 9 of 45 corners, where the three-node seed raises none of the former and fewer of the latter -- see sim/README.md's "#179". The seed does NOT clear #171's solver-diagnostic FAIL gate; the residue is recorded as a finding there, not suppressed.
statistical_convention: N/A (corner-matrix check, not a distribution claim)

analyses: * the testbench carries a .nodeset card seeding the three branch-defining nodes
* (VOUT=1.8, FB=1.2, N_FBB=0.6), so EVERY operating-point solve this deck performs
* -- including the one each `ac` command performs for itself before linearizing --
* is released from that seed instead of from ngspice's unconstrained Newton start.
* One card covers all eighteen points: ngspice recomputes the linearization point
* from scratch for each `ac` command, so a per-point seed is neither possible via
* .ic nor needed via .nodeset. `.ic` would be inert here -- ngspice honours it
* only for the TRANSIENT operating point. Only the branch-defining nodes are
* seeded: one static card cannot be right at 0mA, 1mA and 50mA at once, and the
* eleven-node variant was measured to push ss/-40C/3.63V's 1mA point onto a
* non-regulating branch. The `op` before each `ac` is the same solve the `ac`
* then repeats (same circuit state, same seed, same solver), recorded as
* vout_seed_* so the record itself evidences which branch each of the eighteen
* #338: the grid is now 18 legs = C_eff {0.33,4.7uF} x ESR {0,10m,500m} x load {50mA,1mA,0mA}.
* ESR is the CCVS HESR (V = gain * I(VESRSENSE)), walked with `alter hesr gain = ...`.
* A resistor cannot represent ESR = 0 here: ngspice silently replaces a 0-ohm resistor
* with a ~1 mOhm floor (measured), whereas a CCVS with gain exactly 0 is an exact short.
* Legs 1-7 keep their original order and identities (ac1..ac7 / op1..op7).

measurements.name: pm_c033_50ma_deg
measurements.note: Phase margin at DR-002's low-C_eff corner: C_out 0.33uF, ESR 10mOhm, 50mA. This is the specific corner issue #25 was told to re-check -- the candidate fix screened during #22 showed a 351mV pp limit cycle here. Ratified bound: spec/target-spec.md "Stability" row, PM >= 45 deg worst corner.

measurements.name: gm_c033_50ma_db
measurements.note: Gain margin at the same low-C_eff corner. Ratified bound: spec/target-spec.md "Stability" row, GM >= 10 dB worst corner.

measurements.name: fc_c033_50ma_hz
measurements.note: Unity-loop-gain crossover frequency at the low-C_eff corner. Reported, not bounded: the ratified spec states no bandwidth row. It is the number C_COMP/R_CZ were actually sized against (crossover has to stay below the pass stage's own gm_pass/(2*pi*C_out) pole across the window).

measurements.name: dcgain_c033_50ma_db
measurements.note: DC loop gain at the low-C_eff corner (evaluated at the sweep's 0.01Hz start point). Reported, not bounded: the ratified spec bounds load/line regulation and output accuracy, not loop gain directly.

measurements.name: pm_c033_1ma_deg
measurements.note: Phase margin at C_out 0.33uF, ESR 10mOhm, 1mA. Ratified bound: "Stability" row, PM >= 45 deg.

measurements.name: gm_c033_1ma_db
measurements.note: Gain margin at leg 2 (C_out 0.33uF, ESR 10 mOhm, 1 mA). Ratified bound: "Stability" row, GM >= 10 dB. Added by #338 (boundary-grid expansion).

measurements.name: pm_c033_0ma_deg
measurements.note: Phase margin at C_out 0.33uF, ESR 10mOhm, 0mA (feedback divider is the only preload). Ratified bound: "Stability" row, PM >= 45 deg. Screening at tt/27C says this is the binding point of the whole window -- see design/README.md "Compensation (sized in #25)" and the DR-002 append for why, and for why it is a low-frequency pole/zero doublet dip (gain margin stays very large) rather than a near-oscillation.

measurements.name: gm_c033_0ma_db
measurements.note: Gain margin at the 0mA / 0.33uF point. Recorded alongside pm_c033_0ma_deg specifically because the two tell different stories there: the phase dips into a doublet while the gain is still tens of dB from unity. Ratified bound: "Stability" row, GM >= 10 dB.

measurements.name: vout_seed_p1_v
measurements.note: Operating-point validity gate for leg 1 (#338; evidence role from #179): v(vout) of the seeded operating-point solve that the following `ac` linearizes around. Bounded to 1.62-1.98 V (1.8 V +/- 10%) so that a leg that linearized around a non-regulating branch (e.g. VOUT = VIN or ~0) FAILS the grid instead of yielding a meaningless phase margin. This is a branch-discrimination gate, NOT the ratified Output-accuracy row (other benches own it) and not a relaxation of any spec line.

Bounded to 1.62-1.98 V (1.8 V +/- 10%) so that a leg that linearized around a non-regulating branch (e.g. VOUT = VIN or ~0) FAILS the grid instead of yielding a meaningless phase margin. This is a branch-discrimination gate, NOT the ratified Output-accuracy row (other benches own it) and not a relaxation of any spec line.

ac_leg_grid.esr_representation: CCVS HESR (gain = ESR in ohms, controlled by the 0 V sense source VESRSENSE in series with C_OUT). ESR = 0 is `alter hesr gain = 0`, an exact short; a 0-ohm resistor is NOT used because ngspice silently floors it to ~1 mOhm.
ac_leg_grid.coverage_disclosure: Finite 18-point boundary grid at each PVT corner. Grid coverage (C_eff x ESR x load endpoints) is a different axis from PVT coverage (process/temperature/supply, owned by the corner runner) and neither is a continuous-window qualification: no interior C_eff/ESR/load points are sampled, so endpoint passes do not prove stability over the whole window. Records minted before #338 contain only the original 7 legs and lack the 11 added legs.
